title: confiture verify-checksums --format json
description: File-integrity verification of applied migrations: SHA-256 of each migration file compared against the checksum stored when it was applied. Detects files modified after application. Distinct from `migrate verify`, which checks runtime state via .verify.sql sidecars. Added in 0.39.0 (#189). Consumers read ok (⇔ summary.mismatched == 0) and issues[]. Exit code is 1 when mismatches are found — a success-signal, not an error — so a crash (config/DB error, or an absent ledger without --allow-uninitialized) emits the error envelope (error-envelope.schema.json) instead of this shape. NOT part of the fraisier adapter contract.

ok.description: True when no checksum mismatch was found. Equivalent to summary.mismatched == 0.

ledger_present.description: Whether the migration ledger table (tracking_table, default tb_confiture) exists. False is only emitted under --allow-uninitialized; without that flag an absent ledger raises PRECON_1001 (exit 2) with the error envelope. Distinct from a present-but-empty ledger, which reports true with summary.checked 0. Spelled ledger_present, not tb_confiture_present, because the table name is configurable (#190).

fixed.description: Number of stored checksums rewritten to match the current files. Present only when --fix was passed.

checked.description: Applied migrations whose checksums were compared. 0 when the ledger is absent.

mismatched.description: Applied migrations whose file no longer matches its stored checksum.

tracking_table.description: The resolved ledger name actually queried — the configured tracking_table, not necessarily the tb_confiture default.

issues.description: One entry per checksum mismatch, using the shared issue object. Empty on a clean run.
